review_notes: I read the whole file and checked how FlowEntryProgram, FlowLoopProgram and FlowMatrixBounds use its lemmas. The file has no @[simp] attributes. It has computable definitions (updateRow, updateMatrix, prepareAugment, augment, advance) and their polynomial-time realizer lemmas. The only semantic lemmas are updateMatrix_code, search_residual_nonnegative and advance_code. updateMatrix_code carries the hypothesis hnew, which is not a simp-friendly side condition. Its left side is a specific encoded tuple, and no downstream file uses it through simp. advance_code is used in FlowLoopProgram with an explicit `exact`, and updateMatrix_code is used with an explicit `rw` inside advance_code. Neither is used as a simp lemma. The proofs use `simp only` with explicit lemma lists, so I found no unwanted expansion, competing rules or rewrite cycles. The `change` step in advance_code is a local definitional unfolding, not clear evidence that a canonical simp lemma is missing. Making the defs or the _code lemmas @[simp] would risk unwanted unfolding of the realizer definitions. I did not run Lean, so I can't rule out simp-related issues that only show up when a proof is elaborated.
